text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a software development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers integrate their work many times a day. The core of CI is the automated build, which compiles the code every time a change is made. Following this, a CI pipeline automatically runs a series of tests on the new code. The main goal is catching issues early, before they become large and complicated problems. If a test fails, the team is immediately notified, allowing them to fix the error quickly. This approach reduces integration conflicts and keeps the software stable and reliable throughout the development process.
